neighbours.label: The word right after a body-part noun in a general explanatory claim about anatomy ('tusks are', 'any muscle in the body', 'cells you have'), vs the same sentence frames about non-body objects
fire: A giraffe's legs are long enough to kick a lion away.
Like every bone in the body, the skull keeps renewing itself.
The tongue is one of the strongest muscles you have.
A cat's whiskers are really sensitive touch organs.
Like any tendon in the body, it tears if it is overloaded.
Your liver is the largest internal organ you have.
A shark's teeth are replaced throughout its life.
As with any joint in the body, the knee needs regular movement.
quiet: A giraffe's paddock is large enough for three adults.
Like every house on the street, the cottage needs a new roof.
The Nile is one of the longest rivers you can visit.
A cat's basket is really just an old wooden crate.
Like any bridge in the city, it closes if the wind is strong.
Your garage is the largest storage space you have.
A shark's tank is cleaned twice a week at the aquarium.
As with any road in the region, the pass needs regular repairs.

predictions: Anatomy claims reach 0.3-0.7 on the word after the body-part noun; matching frames about places or objects stay under 0.12.
short: word after body-part noun in anatomy claim
notes: Card: elephant tusks are, any muscle in the body, delicate senses you have, plus guns on the planet and code.
